messages:
marina: Heads up — ran a cross-host perf probe on the PP bubble + 1F1B stack. Seeing a 28% p50 token latency regression and ~18% throughput drop when async all-reduce is enabled across hosts. Repro steps below.
aj: yikes. do you have the profiling traces? nvprof / nsight or our perf flame graphs?
devin: can you paste the kernel selection log? last time a kernel fallback to a slower warp schedule caused the same shape.
marina: attaching the quick log snippet: 
```
[INFO] kernel: selected matmul_kernel_fused_fp16_v2 for layer 18
[WARN] fallback: kernel matmul_fp16_small -> matmul_fp32_generic (latency +3.2ms)
[INFO] allreduce: nccl async on, cross-host route via ring-2
[PERF] microbatch=8, pp_stages=4, 1f1b=true, kv_cache_hits=92%
```
rishi: kv_cache_hits 92% is fine but if the early layers have high parameter fanout we still see extra gradient chatter. did you isolate by disabling kv-cache?
emma: quick experiment: try microbatch=4 and enable contiguous kernel packing + fused-allreduce. that reduced bubble we saw before. command: `rdwctl run --microbatch 4 --pp 4 --fuse-allreduce`
marina: tried microbatch=4 locally (single-host) — bubble shrank, throughput +12% but cross-host still bad. suspect NCCL scheduling + unexpected kernel mixes.
devin: I want the per-stage compute vs comm breakdown. can you upload the trace to /tmp/prof-195432 and ping the perf-bucket? buildbot: uploaded trace to gs://redwood-perf/profiles/195432_prof.tar.gz and posted a short summary.
buildbot: summary: stage0 compute 4.2ms | allreduce 1.1ms, stage1 compute 5.0ms | allreduce 3.8ms (cross-host increased by 3.2ms), imbalance at stage1->stage2 transitions.
aj: that stage1 allreduce spike aligns with a kernel fallback on layer 22 in your log — different kernels give different message sizes and NCCL chooses a different algorithm.
devin: actionable: force consistent kernel selection across replicas (disable the slow fallback) and force NCCL to use tree algorithm for cross-host. test both independently.
marina: running two experiments now: (A) pin kernel to matmul_kernel_fused_fp16_v2 via env RKERNEL_PREF=matmul_kernel_fused_fp16_v2 (B) set NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_TOPO=cross_host_force_tree. will post numbers in ~40m.
rishi: also check for tiny allreduce fragmentation — small tensor shapes get coalesced badly when microbatching is low. maybe aggregation window size needs bump.
emma: note: if you increase aggregation window you can reduce allreduce count but increase per-req latency; tradeoff for tail-sensitive workloads.
marina: quick interim: experiment A (kernel pin) results: p50 token latency down 14% vs baseline, throughput +9%. Experiment B (tree algo) results: p50 latency down 10%, throughput +7%. combined A+B: p50 down 30%, throughput +22% (cross-host).
aj: nice. any regression on memory or kv-cache behavior when forcing kernel?
marina: memory steady. kv-cache hits unchanged. interestingly, forcing kernel removed a small GC_yield spike we saw in traces (likely because fallback was using slower ops that serialized).
devin: next steps: add a safeguard in runtime: prefer stable kernel families when cross-host routing is used OR auto-switch NCCL algo when we detect small-allreduce hotspots. open a PR with a feature flag for a week canary.
emma: also add a perf test in CI that runs a minimal cross-host 1F1B with microbatch=8 and fails if p50 regresses >5% from baseline.
marina: will open the issue + PR. I'll drop the raw traces + command lines in the issue. thanks all :thumbsup:
